judgment.notes: Unique integer definition n=lambda+1; no positivity or dimension is assumed by naming n. Positivity and its identification with dimension/cardinality are exported by N001. Compatible with the original lambda range and all uses as a finite rank.

I is the bounded integer interval with both endpoints included, well-defined and finite even before a nonemptiness claim. Conversion of nonnegative indices/factorial arguments to naturals is explicit. H001 and N001, not the definition, provide nonemptiness and cardinality lambda+1. No endpoint is lost at lambda=0.

Typed family I -> V with the original divided-power normalization e_i=y^i v/i!. Indices in I are nonnegative and factorials are nonzero in C, so the formula is legitimate; zero power is specified. It does not assume v belongs to M or that e is a basis. Basis existence and e_0=v are separately exported in N001 before coordinate constructions.

X_r=x^r/r! is defined only for nonnegative integer r as a complex-linear operator. Factorial division is over C, not over K, and X_0 is the identity. No integrality or lattice-preservation property is smuggled into the definition; these are distinct N001/N002 clauses. Reduction identities over K are restricted to r<=lambda

Y_r=y^r/r! has the same legitimate characteristic-zero domain as X, including Y_0=Id. The normalization agrees with the problem. It makes no assertion about M or reduction; preservation and permitted division after reduction are explicitly separate statements, avoiding division by p! in K.

Defines the integer subalgebra in the abstract complex enveloping algebra, with explicitly introduced raising/lowering generators and their representation images X,Y. D015 fixes which abstract generators are meant. This faithfully resolves the original use of x,y both abstractly and as operators, without assuming the representation faithful (important at lambda=0). Lattice stability is H004, not a conclusion of this definition; the consuming R002 has H002 and H004 as direct inputs.

R is exactly the rational subring Z_(p) with nonzero integer denominators not divisible by p and the usual embedding into C. H001 is an explicit guard and a direct input of every R using R. Closure under products and sums is addressed in R002; localization and unit assertions are not made true by the name Z_(p), but supplied in the later arguments/statements. Nonzero denominator convention removes ambiguity.
